$comment: govkit guardrail manifest. Written by /govkit-init, read by /govkit-doctor and /govkit config. This file is the DECLARED state; the doctor compares it against what is actually on disk and reports the difference. A guardrail you deliberately do not want is recorded here with enabled:false and a reason — so a missing guardrail is always either a recorded decision or a finding, never an accident.

release-gate.description: Local CI-fallback gate for when Actions minutes run out
release-gate.$comment: The gate is NOT owned by govkit — release-gate-kit is canonical. govkit vendors a copy so init works offline, and records the upstream version here. The doctor compares this version, NOT the file bytes: every project runs its own formatter, so a byte comparison would report drift on every repo that uses Prettier and be ignored within a week.

ci.description: CI running the same checks as the release gate

pre-push-hook.description: Blocks direct pushes to the release branch. On a private repo under a free plan this is the ONLY enforcement — GitHub saves a protection rule there but does not enforce it.

doc-sync.description: Per-PR watchdog: code changed without its mapped doc

docs-sync-check.description: Per-session: bootstrap-doc freshness + git/gh ground truth
docs-sync-check.$comment: watchedPaths deliberately excludes docs/ — updating one doc must not mark every other doc stale, or the check cries wolf and gets ignored.

branches.$comment: The pre-push hook protects `release`. Merge strategy follows branch shape: a long-lived working->release pair takes MERGE COMMITS, never squash — squashing writes a new SHA with no ancestry link, so the release branch stops containing the working branch and every later PR replays already-merged commits.
